previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with severe psoriatic arthritis and multiple comorbidities was admitted for acute left leg and knee pain. He presented with a flare of his arthritis, including swelling and severe pain in the left knee, with radiating symptoms to the calf. Imaging ruled out fracture and DVT, and arthrocentesis revealed inflammatory fluid with no crystals or infection. Empiric antibiotics were started but discontinued after cultures remained negative. Prednisone was increased to 60 mg daily, resulting in significant improvement. He developed mild calf pain, which was monitored and attributed to inflammatory or neuropathic causes; gabapentin was initiated. A cervical trigger point injection was performed for headache, and he maintained good glycemic control on his insulin regimen. He was discharged home with a prednisone taper, continued immunosuppression, and follow-up arranged with rheumatology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with left foot swelling, had negative ultrasound
two days ago, but needs repeat to evaluate for DVT.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound of the left extremity from ___ and
unilateral lower extremity veins of the left from ___.

FINDINGS:

Gray-scale and Doppler images of the left lower extremity were obtained.  Left
and right common femoral, left superficial femoral, popliteal, and proximal
calf veins.  All veins showed normal response to compression and augmentation
with wall-to-wall flow.  No DVT was present.  There is a large complex fluid
collection along the left posterior medial calf extending down below the
gastrocnemius.  This fluid is of unknown origin given the fact that there was
no ___ cyst two days ago.

IMPRESSION:

No left lower extremity DVT present.  Large left posterior calf fluid
collection.  Recommend MRI for further evaluation.

HISTORY:  Left leg swelling and fluid collection.  Evaluate osteomyelitis
infection.

TECHNIQUE:  Imaging performed at 1.5 Tesla using body array coil.  Axial T1,
T2, and STIR, sagittal T1, axial pre-contrast fat saturated T1-weighted
spoiled gradient echo, and post-contrast axial 3D T1-weighted spoiled gradient
echo, fat saturated T1-weighted spin echo, and sagittal 3D T1-weighted spoiled
gradient echo images through the left knee were obtained.

LEFT CALF MRI WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST:

There are two multiloculated high T2 collections, with somewhat thick rims of
enhancement, in the proximal mid/calf, one in the popliteus muscle and the
other abutting the medial gastrocnemius muscle.  The first collection lies
within the substance of the popliteus muscle and measures ~ 14.4 x 25.1
(axial) x 3.4 mm, with edema in the surrounding muscle. The second fluid
collection is centered in the fat plane between the soleus and medial
gastrocnemius muscle, and extends inferiorly along the posteromedial edge of
the gastrocnemius muscle, likely deep to the crural fascia.  It measures ~
14.4 x 25.1 (axial) x 3.4 mm. This latter collection deforms the gastrocnemius
muscle to a small degree. Some of this fluid collection may invaginate into
the medial edge of the gastrocnemius muscle and there is minimal edema and
enhancement in the surrounding muscle (series 3, image 31)

There is edema extending along the fat plane between the popliteus muscle,
soleus, and medial gastrocnemius and extending along the posterior aspect of
the gastrocnemius muscle.  There is diffuse subcutaneous edema about the calf.

Muscles are otherwise within normal limits. No evidence of osteomyelitis.

Assessment of the knee is quite limited on these views, as the field of view
for the body array coil does not extend effectively beyond the calf itself.
There is a small  knee joint effusion.  No obvious direct communication
between these collections  and the knee joint effusion is identified, but the
popliteus abscess does extend along the popliteus tendon, which can
communicate with the knee in some patients. Full assessment of the
relationship between the knee joint and popliteus is limited on these views.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Two loculated fluid collections concerning for abcess collections, one in
the substance of the popliteus muscle, and the other along the anteromedial
edge of the medial gastrocnemius muscle.

2. Subcutaneous edema likely represents cellulitis in this setting.

3. No evidence of osteomyelitis.

4. Limited assessment of knee joint -- please see comment.

INDICATION:  ___ man with left knee abscess.

PROCEDURE:  The risks, benefits and procedures were explained to the patient
and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedural timeout was
performed confirming patient identity, site and side of procedure to be
performed.  The patient was placed supine on the fluoroscopic table.  Initial
ultrasound images demonstrate a complex multiloculated fluid collection in the
left calf with a medial superficial component corresponding to the MRI
abnormality.  

The area over the medial, superficial component was prepped and draped in
standard sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine was used to anesthetize skin and
subcutaneous tissues.  Under ultrasound guidance, a 15-gauge needle was
advanced into the fluid collection and approximately 7 cc of purulent material
aspirated.  These were sent for cell count, culture, AFB and fungal stain. 
The needle was removed, hemostasis achieved, and a sterile dry bandage placed.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and experienced no immediate
complications.

The patient left the department in good condition.

The procedure was supervised by Dr. ___, attending.  

IMPRESSION:  Successful ultrasound-guided aspiration of 7 cc of purulent
material from the left mid calf abscess.  Samples were sent for cell count,
culture, AFB and fungal stain.

INDICATION:  ___ man with bacteremia status post aspiration of left
lower extremity fluid collection, now with posterior knee pain and anterior
tibial pain.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound-guided drainage of left leg of ___ and
left leg ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:  A large complex fluid collection is again seen in the left
popliteal fossa tracking down the medial left calf.  The overall ___
and geography of this collection are difficult to assess with ultrasound.  No
vascular flow is identified within this collection.

A second small fluid collection is seen at the anterior left knee.  This
collection measures 3.5 x 3.2 x 1.1 cm.

Grayscale, color, and Doppler images were obtained of the left common femoral,
superficial femoral, popliteal and tibial veins.  There is normal flow,
compression and augmentation seen in all of the vessels.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Large complex fluid collection tracking from the left popliteal fossa
along the medial left calf to the proximal mid calf region.  Since it is
difficult to fully assess the extent and geography of this collection on
ultrasound, an MRI is suggested for further characterization.
2.  Smaller fluid collection at the left anterior knee measuring 3.5 cm.
3.  No evidence of deep vein thrombosis in the left leg.

TYPE OF EXAMINATION:  Chest AP portable single view.

INDICATION:  ___ male patient with infection, check location of
left-sided PICC line.

FINDINGS:  A left-sided PICC line is identified and seen to terminate
overlying the SVC at the level 1.5 cm above the carina.  No pneumothorax has
developed and no new infiltrates are seen.

IMPRESSION:  Acceptable position of PICC line.

HISTORY:  Evaluate gastrocnemius abscess following drainage for interval
change.

COMPARISON:  MRI of the left calf from ___, and ultrasound of
the left calf, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contrast-enhanced axial CT of the left calf was performed.
Sagittal and coronal reconstructions were performed.

FINDINGS:

There is a loculated, peripherally enhancing fluid extending around, or within
the popliteus muscle/popliteus sheath measures 2.8 cm (TV) x 1.8 cm (AP) x 5.0
cm (CC), not significantly changed.  

A second loculated fluid collection interposed between the medial head of the
gastrocnemius muscle and the semimembranosus tendon extending inferiorly and
posteriorly along the anterior aspect of the medial head of the gastrocnemius
muscle now contains several foci of air from recent aspiration.  Portions of
this collection are inseparable from the anterior muscle fibers of medial head
of the gastrocnemius muscle.  

This multiloculated  measures approximately 12 cm in length, slightly
increased since the previous study (measured approximately 9 cm when measured
in a similar fashion on the previous) and is composed of three dominant
locules. The most superiorly located locule along the anterior aspect of the
medial gastrocnemius muscle measures 1.8 cm (TV) x 1.2 cm (AP).  More
inferiorly located locule along the anterior aspect of the medial
gastrocnemius muscle measures 1.3 cm (TV) x 2.5 cm (AP).  These two locules
are not significantly changed in size.  A third locule of fluid more
inferiorly at the anterior aspect of the gastrocnemius muscle measuring
approximately 2.1 cm (AP) x 1.3 cm (TV) is new since the previous MRI.   

Subcutaneous edema is seen along the anterior aspect of the tibial diaphysis,
not significantly changed.

The tibia and fibula are normal in appearance. MInimal knee joint effusion
noted.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Redemonstration of two loculated fluid collections in the left calf.
Slightly increased inferior extent of the collection along the anteromedial
edge of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.  Otherwise no significant
change. 
2.  Subcutaneous edema along the anterior left leg, in keeping with
cellulitis, unchanged.
3. Small loculates of air within the lower collection is attributed to recent
aspiration procedure. No other evidence of soft tissue emphysema identified.

INDICATION:  ___ male with left lower extremity fluid collections, for
preoperative marking.

COMPARISON:  CT lower extremity ___ and MR calf ___.

FINDINGS: Once again, a heterogeneously hypoechoic fluid collection centered
in the popliteus muscle extends from the popliteal fossa along the medial
aspect of the proximal calf, at a depth ranging from 1.6 to 2.3 cm. In the
popliteal fossa, this collection measures up to 2.3 cm on transverse images. A
second separate second collection measuring up to 2.8 cm on transverse images
in the medial subcutaneous tissues extends along the proximal-to-mid calf at a
depth ranging from 2.6 to 2.2. As requested, markings were made on the skin
delineating the distribution of these collection and their depths. 

IMPRESSION:  Two separate left calf fluid collections, preoperatively marked. 

Discussed with Dr. ___.

HISTORY:  Preoperative.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is again prominence of
the cardiac silhouette, some of which may be related to the low lung volumes. 
However, no evidence of vascular congestion, pleural effusion, or acute focal
pneumonia.

INDICATION:  ___ man with atraumatic left leg pain.  Recently
underwent debridement of left calf.

COMPARISON:  ___ and ___.

LEFT LOWER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND:  Gray-scale, color, and Doppler ultrasound
was used to evaluate the left common femoral, superficial femoral, and
popliteal veins.  Calf veins could not be evaluated due to the presence of an
overlying dressing.  The right common femoral vein was also assessed.  There
is normal compressibility, flow and augmentation between the left popliteal
and left common femoral veins.  In the popliteal fossa, a complex fluid
collection is again noted.  Its most caudal extent is not visualized, as it
extends below the dressing.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of left lower extremity DVT between the left popliteal and
common femoral veins.

2.  Left popliteal fossa collection extending into the calf, again seen.

INDICATION:  ___ man with psoriatic arthritis, on immunosuppression. 
Gastrocnemius abscess.

FINDINGS:  Comparison is made to prior ultrasound performed ___.  A 6.1
cm x 1.4 cm x 2.2 cm hypoechoic area in the left popliteal fossa extending
into the left posterior calf has not changed significantly in size since prior
ultrasound.  This is consistent with a fluid collection and contains multiple
small hyperechoic areas which were not present on the prior scan, most likely
representing small foci of gas.  

IMPRESSION:

No significant change in size of fluid collection in the left popliteal fossa
extending into the left posterior calf, which contains small foci of gas.

HISTORY:  Psoriatic arthritis on immunosuppression with gastrocnemius
abscesses and overlying cellulitis status post incision and drainage with knee
pain.

COMPARISON:  Preprocedural MRI from ___, and CT of the left calf
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar MRI of the left calf was performed prior to and
following the uneventful administration of intravenous gadolinium.

FINDINGS:

There has been incision and drainage in the medial calf since the previous
study and there is an open wound over the medial aspect of the medial head of
the gastrocnemius muscle.  The open wound is in contiguity with a rim-
enhancing fluid collection posterior to the medial head of the gastrocnemius
muscle, but demonstrates internal low signal intensity which may be from air
or possibly packing material or less likely hemosiderin.  This collection
measures 7.5 cm (TV) x 1.4 cm (AP) x 11 cm (CC).

Again seen in the popliteus muscle is a rim-enhancing fluid collection that
measures 2 cm (TV) x 1 cm (AP) x 2.6 cm (CC), slightly decreased in
craniocaudal length since the CT (previously measured 5 cm in length). Rim-
enhancing collection at the anterior aspect of the medial head of the
gastrocnemius, again demonstrating two loculated components is not
significantly changed; however, the inferior most aspect of this fluid
collection is not included in the field of view.  The more laterally located
fluid pocket of this collection at the anteromedial aspect of the medial head
of the gastrocnemius muscle measures 1.5 cm (TV) x 0.8 cm (AP) x approximately
11 cm in craniocaudal length, however, the inferior aspect of this collection
is not included.  More medially located locule of this collection measures 1.5
cm (TV) x 0.8 cm (AP).

There is a edema in the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle and in the
vastus medialis obliquus muscle, new since the preoperative study and likely
due to the recent surgery.  Diffuse subcutaneous edema is seen throughout the
leg, predominantly at the posterior and lateral aspects.  This study was not
tailored for evaluation of the menisci or ligaments, however, diffuse
intrinsic signal abnormality is seen throughout the medial meniscus,
predominantly in the posterior horn and intrasubstance signal abnormality is
seen in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.  Trace subchondral bone
marrow edema is seen in the superior aspect of the patella.  There is mild
thickening in intrinsic signal abnormality in the distal patellar tendon,
suggestive of tendinosis.

There is a small-to-moderate sized joint effusion, which demonstrates synovial
thickening and enhancement, in keeping with synovitis.  There is
cartilage thinning and subchondral cysts along the median eminence of
the patella. There are no osseous cortical erosions in the articular surfaces
of the tibia or femur. Trace, nonspecific bone marrow edema is seen in the
anterior and posterior tibial plateaus.

Subcentimeter popliteal reactive lymph node is seen.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Persisted popliteus muscle collection and collection at the anteromedial
aspect of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.

2.  Post-surgical findings following incision and drainage is a new collection
posterior to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, contiguous with the
medial open skin defect and contains low signal intensity foci, which may be
due to air or possibly packing.

3.  Muscle edema in the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle and vastus
medialis obliquus muscle, likely postoperative.

4.  A small knee joint effusion and mild synovitis without definite findings
of septic arthritis. As previously noted, the popliteus tendon sheath can
communicate with the knee joint. Cartilage thinning and subchondral cysts
along patella may be degenerative. Clinical correlation is requested.

INDICATION:  ___ male with altered mental status (somnolent), status
post unwitnessed fall in room.  Evaluate for acute process.

COMPARISON:  MR of ___ and CT head ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain without IV
contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were displayed.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, infarction, mass effect or
edema.  The gray-white matter differentiation is preserved.  Ventricles and
sulci are normal in size and appearance.  The basilar cisterns are preserved. 
Globes and lens are intact.  The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air
cells are well aerated.  No osseous abnormality is identified.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial abnormality.

Right PICC tip is very difficult to visualize can be followed to the lower SVC
